title: URL and typosquat spotting
description: Compare lookalike hostnames, punycode, and risky TLDs against the real Northwind and PayPal-style brands used in this lab. All hostnames are simulated.
learningObjectives: Detect digit and character substitutions in brand-like domains
Treat punycode (xn--) as something to decode, not as proof of safety
Flag disposable or unusual TLDs in unsolicited messages
Compare displayed link text to the real hostname

steps.title: Lookalike brand domain
steps.prompt: Which hostname is a lookalike of paypal.com (digit or character substitution)?
steps.hint: Compare letter by letter with paypal.com — watch for 1 vs l.

steps.title: Punycode decoding
steps.prompt: What punycode (xn--) hostname is stored for the internationalized lookalike URL?
steps.hint: Engine → artifacts → URL entries list punycode even when the UI shows Unicode.

steps.title: Risky TLD
steps.prompt: Which TLD on the invoice lure is commonly treated as higher risk in this training set?
steps.hint: Compare the options to the hostname on the lure link.

steps.title: What to do next
steps.prompt: You found a lookalike domain and a risky TLD. What is the best next action in this training scenario?
choices: Click through to verify the page looks real
Report / quarantine and do not use the link
Reply to the sender asking if it is legitimate
expected: Report / quarantine and do not use the link

hints: A Latin 'l' and digit '1' are easy to miss at small font sizes.
Punycode is a representation of Unicode domains — decode it before trusting the brand.
Never verify a suspicious link by opening it on a production machine; use the training Engine panel instead.
